newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Terrified Clinton plays golf with Norman.
newsitem.headline: Terrified Clinton plays golf with Norman.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton fulfilled a duffer's dream on Thursday when he took to the fairways with Australian golfing legend Greg Norman.
Teeing off at the New South Wales Golf Club, Clinton was asked how he felt playing with the world number one. "Terrified," he said with a smile.
When asked what his primary goal was, Clinton replied: "Stay out of trouble."
Clinton patiently stood over his ball and swung hard, hooking the ball. "Too far left," he muttered.

Norman, standing behind the president, asked: "Are you going to take another?" Clinton, an avid amateur with a fondness for "mulligans" -- which let a player try again without it appearing in his score -- replied: "Are you going to count it?"

Both men laughed, and the ground rules were clear. Clinton set up another ball and hit it down the fairway. Norman, known as "The Shark" because of extraordinary competitiveness, needed only one swing to put his ball where he wanted it.
The two also played with John Coates, president of Australia's Olympic Committee, and Ted Kunkel, chief executive officer of the Fosters beer company.
Earlier on Thursday, Norman took an early first-round lead at the Australian Open on another Sydney course, picking up six birdies to end the round at five under par.
